description: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Optimisations applied,” compares the performance of two models—“NESAC ft model” (orange bars) and “SESHE ft model” (green bars)—across five different optimisation techniques: “Normalised,” “Add Spacing,” “Remove Spacing,” “Americanisms,” and “Dates.” The vertical axis lists these optimisations in descending order of their performance values, from highest to lowest. The horizontal axis, labeled “Model,” represents the performance metric, which is scaled linearly from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. Each optimisation has two bars, one for each model, with the exact performance value labeled at the end of each bar. The “Normalised” optimisation yields the highest performance for both models, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00334 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00323. The “Add Spacing” optimisation follows, with values of 0.00319 and 0.00344 respectively. The “Remove Spacing” optimisation shows values of 0.00311 and 0.00306. The “Americanisms” optimisation results in 0.00299 and 0.00302. The “Dates” optimisation yields the lowest performance, with 0.00257 for the NESAC ft model and 0.00228 for the SESHA ft model. The bars are grouped by optimisation, with the NESAC ft model’s bar appearing above the SESHA ft model’s bar for each category. There is no visual emphasis or sorting beyond the descending order of the optimisations on the y-axis.
